solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Token rebellion feasible

parts.note: a coup is a sudden rebellion that seizes power
on, as in 'that's not on', means possible or feasible

explanation.surface: A small gesture of revolt that might actually work.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher or ticket exchangeable for goods, which is a kind of token.

clue.text: What gets kept in wardrobe — little daggers!

indicators.note: the answer is something kept inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: Someone discovers tiny knives stashed in a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little daggers' looks like the definition, but 'little' supplies the last two letters of the run: wardrOBE LIttle.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, the dagger symbol is also called an obelus; the plural form names several such marks.

clue.text: Soldier needing rest, one about to become dependant on others

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to sit is to rest
I is the Roman numeral for one
C (circa) is short for about, used with dates

explanation.surface: A weary soldier, taking a break, starts to lean on everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasitic creature or person lives off others, relying on them for support.

clue.text: Worry's little good in Scottish town that's been upset

indicators.note: the letter for good is placed inside the overturned town name
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the town's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland
G is a short form of good

explanation.surface: A minor goodness in a Scottish town that has been disturbed causes concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been upset' turns ELGIN into NIGLE; 'in' then puts G inside it, after NIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To niggle is to cause slight but persistent worry or irritation.

clue.text: Commander glared and went red

parts.note: CO is short for Commanding Officer
to lour (or lower) is to scowl or glare

explanation.surface: A commanding officer scowled and then blushed with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured as a verb in the past tense means blushed, became flushed in the face.

clue.text: An all-star ball

parts.note: reads like a glamorous dance attended only by celebrities, but means the imaginary globe on which all the stars appear to lie

explanation.surface: A glittering dance with an all-celebrity guest list.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers picture the sky as a vast imaginary sphere around the Earth on which every star is projected.

clue.text: Address for posh female (the woman's cool!)

parts.note: lady's means belonging to the woman
hip means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: An aside about how a society lady should be addressed, with a remark on her style.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Her Ladyship' is the respectful form of address for a titled woman.

clue.text: Member of family has dirty article thrown away

indicators.note: the article is discarded from the longer word for dirty

parts.note: unclean means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A relative owns a filthy item that gets binned.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a relative, a brother of one's parent.

clue.text: Teachers in red coats moving around university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the university letter
the letters of red coats are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Lecturers wearing scarlet jackets walking around campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges RED COATS into EDCATORS; 'around' puts it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Educators is a general word for teachers.

clue.text: Untidy item of furniture, tattered, left for collection

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture

indicators.note: the word for tattered gathers up, or collects, the letter for left

parts.note: ragged means tattered

explanation.surface: A shabby old bed, all in tatters, has been put out for the refuse collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for collection' has RAGGED collect L, making RAGGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled means dishevelled and messy in appearance.

clue.text: Foolish person falling short as a friend

indicators.note: the word for a fool is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a chump is a fool

explanation.surface: A remark that a silly person makes a poor friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is an informal word for a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Rex is having fish, the ultimate in delicious fried food

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
taken as written
sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter of delicious is taken

explanation.surface: A man called Rex orders fish and calls it the best fried food going.
explanation.definitionFit: Rissoles are fried cakes of minced meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Notice was about something in the playground

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: about indicates the word was is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an object in the play area.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a long plank pivoted in the middle, standard equipment in a children's playground.

clue.text: Dreary accommodation

definitions.meaning: an apartment, a place to live

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the word: dull and lacking interest, and a set of rooms on one floor to live in.

clue.text: Smooth ale is horrible, disgusting

indicators.note: a horrible version of the words is a mangled one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A beer drinker complains that a supposedly smooth ale tastes revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means arousing hatred or disgust, a synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: I am the bee's knees, a short Conservative ape

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
it, as in 'he thinks he's it', means the very best, like the bee's knees
taken as written

indicators.note: the word for a Conservative loses its last letter

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A boastful short Tory claims to be the best, while merely copying others.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, so as a noun an ape is a copier, a mimic.

clue.text: Desperate man overwhelmed by a smell rising up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the man is swamped, enclosed, by the letters around him

parts.note: a scent is a smell
Desperate Dan is the strongman hero of the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A frantic man is overcome by a rising stench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' looks like an anagram signal, but Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendant means rising, climbing upwards in position or influence.

clue.text: Voice of gangster in loud quarrel

indicators.note: the gangster goes inside the combined letters for loud and quarrel

parts.note: f (forte) is the musical direction for loud
a set-to is a fight or quarrel
Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster's voice rises during a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a male singing voice pitched above the normal range.

clue.text: Jazz fan at front of cold concert venue missing nothing

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a devotee

indicators.note: the first letter of cold is taken

parts.note: a hall is where concerts are held

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast arrives at a chilly concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch-all covers every case, leaving nothing out.

clue.text: Son in bed suffering

indicators.note: the son is placed inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A sick son lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cost can mean loss or suffering, as in 'to my cost'.

clue.text: Frank the composer, born on hilltop

parts.note: a ridge is the crest of a hill

explanation.surface: A biographical note on a composer born on a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bridge was an English composer and the teacher of Benjamin Britten.

clue.text: Containers placed around hospital? I'm so grateful!

indicators.note: the containers go round the hospital letter

parts.note: tanks are containers for liquids
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone thanks the people who put containers around a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanks as an exclamation expresses gratitude.

clue.text: Man on board losing his head when the stars appear

indicators.note: the chess piece loses its first letter

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

explanation.surface: A chess piece loses its head after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, when the stars become visible.

clue.text: Friend collecting a payment as one looking after the kids?

definitions.text: as one looking after the kids?

indicators.note: the friend gathers in the other letters

parts.note: pal means friend
taken as written
rent is a regular payment for a property

explanation.surface: A friend picks up a payment for childminding.
explanation.definitionFit: Parental describes acting as a parent, the role of one bringing up children.

clue.text: Rep's time with heritage organisation

parts.note: an age is a period of time
NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic British buildings

explanation.surface: A sales rep takes time off to visit a heritage site.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep (representative) acts as agent for a company.

clue.text: Medal disappearing, one lost

indicators.note: the letter for one is lost from the word for disappearing

parts.note: going means vanishing, as in 'going, going, gone'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A medal has vanished, leaving one fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or award.

clue.text: Get nowhere, being wet?

parts.note: a swimmer keeping afloat in one spot is literally getting nowhere while wet, and the idiom means making no progress

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the rain making no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To make no progress is the idiomatic sense, from staying upright in deep water without moving forward.

clue.text: Others around me in accommodation for the elderly

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of others are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Others gather round the speaker in an old people's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residential care home for elderly people.

clue.text: English country property

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: An English country house and its grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large property, typically a house and its land.
